title: When classical ML beats a neural network, which is often

claims.text: Grinsztajn, Oyallon and Varoquaux benchmarked standard and novel deep learning methods against tree-based models across 45 datasets with clear tabular characteristics, with a methodology accounting for both fitting models and finding good hyperparameters, and published the result in the datasets and benchmarks track in 2022.

source.title: Leo Grinsztajn, Edouard Oyallon and Gael Varoquaux, Why do tree-based models still outperform deep learning on typical tabular data?, Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35, Datasets and Benchmarks track, pages 507-520, 2022

claims.text: Their findings were that tree-based models remain state of the art on medium-sized data, of the order of ten thousand samples, even without accounting for their superior speed; that the performance gap is not mostly due to categorical features; and that it does not disappear after tuning hyperparameters. They identify robustness to uninformative features as a desirable inductive bias for tabular data.

source.title: Leo Grinsztajn, Edouard Oyallon and Gael Varoquaux, Why do tree-based models still outperform deep learning on typical tabular data?, Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35, Datasets and Benchmarks track, pages 507-520, 2022

beats.broke: the methods that transformed perception problems are assumed to be the strongest option everywhere, so they get reached for on problems whose structure is nothing like an image or a sentence
beats.fix: match the method to the structure of the data — tabular columns are heterogeneous, individually meaningful and often uninformative, which suits models that select among features rather than compose them
beats.cost: the conclusion is empirical and bounded by the regime it was measured in, so it holds for datasets of the size and shape that were benchmarked rather than as a universal rule
beats.interview: why the newer method is not the default choice on tabular data
